Command: Offer a sin offering for inadvertent sin
Summary: The command: Offer a sin offering for inadvertent sin (Leviticus 4:27). When one of the common people sinned through ignorance, a female goat or lamb without blemish was his sin offering.
Commandment: Offer a sin offering for inadvertent sin, as prescribed in Leviticus 4:27.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: Even sins committed in ignorance needed blood, and that is what makes this ceremonial: a rite of atonement. Its goal was to cover the common person's inadvertent sin — a female goat or lamb without blemish — so that ignorance did not leave guilt standing. The evil was sin itself, including sin the sinner had not noticed. It restrained that evil by giving it a set remedy: the sin was named, the offering brought, and atonement made.
